title: Optimization config diff engine + semantic validation (batching/cache/quant constraints)
creator: Ethan Park
project: Safe apply + rollback mechanism (Optimization Config versioning)
description:
Context
We’re introducing immutable Optimization Config versions + safe apply/rollback. To make this operationally safe, we need (1) a canonical diff between versions and (2) semantic validators that catch dangerous/invalid changes before rollout (and can be surfaced in Console + API).

This ticket covers:
- Diff computation between two config versions (stable + human-friendly).
- Semantic validation rules for batching heuristics, caching toggles/params, and quantization profile references.
- Actionable error messages + severity levels to drive safe-apply gating UX.

Goals
- Prevent high-risk or invalid config changes from being applied (especially across the wrong blast radius).
- Provide a deterministic diff representation for:
  - Console diff view (highlight riskier fields)
  - Audit log payloads (optional summary)
  - Rollout controller (to decide which validators and gates to run)

Non-goals
- Full policy engine / approvals workflow (handled elsewhere).
- Auto-fixing configs (we only validate and explain).

Requirements
1) Diff engine
- Input: config_version_a, config_version_b (JSON payloads as stored).
- Output:
  - Stable ordering (no noisy diffs due to map order)
  - Path-based changes (e.g., "batching.max_batch_tokens")
  - Change type: add/remove/modify
  - Old/new values stringified safely (truncate large arrays/objects)
  - Optional "risk" annotation per change (low/medium/high) based on field registry.
- Must ignore known non-functional metadata fields (e.g., "description", "labels").
- Must support forward-compat fields (unknown fields should still diff rather than fail).

2) Semantic validators
Validators run during /validate and are also re-run during /apply to protect against TOCTOU (config mutated in DB is not possible, but referenced entities can change).

2a) Batching validators
- Hard bounds (reject):
  - max_batch_tokens within [1k, 256k] (exact numbers from runtime team; see below)
  - max_concurrent_sequences within [1, 4096]
  - target_queue_delay_ms within [0, 200]
- Relationship constraints (reject):
  - max_batch_tokens must be >= max_sequence_length (if provided) + safety margin
  - If "continuous_batching" enabled, require "scheduler" == "rw-continuous" (or compatible)
- Warning-level checks (allow but warn):
  - Raising max_batch_tokens by >2x vs previous version
  - Lowering target_queue_delay_ms to <5ms (risk of throughput collapse)

2b) Cache validators
- Compatibility (reject):
  - prefix_cache.enabled cannot be true if runtime model family lacks KV/prefix cache support (needs runtime capability lookup)
  - cache.max_kv_cache_gb must be <= node allocation cap for the target deployment mode (Hosted/Dedicated vs Private)
  - cache.shard_count must be a power of two and <= 256
- Cross-field (reject):
  - If prefix_cache.enabled true, require "cache.key" contains "model_id" + "tokenizer_hash" to avoid cross-version poisoning.
- Warning-level:
  - Disabling cache when previous version enabled (call out expected p95 impact)
  - Enabling cache for very long context models without "eviction_policy" set

2c) Quantization profile validators
- Reference integrity (reject):
  - quant.profile_id must exist and be in state "promoted" for customer-facing apply (internal overrides allowed behind feature flag)
  - quant.profile_id must be compatible with model_id (arch + tensor parallelism + weights format)
- Quality guardrails (warn/reject depending on scope):
  - If quant profile changes (profile_id differs from previous), mark change as "high risk" and require eval gate configured for apply unless scope is a single canary shard.
- Private deployment nuance:
  - If mode==Private and quant.profile_source=="remote", reject (air-gapped default); allow with explicit override flag.

3) Error model + API surface expectations
- /validate returns:
  - ok boolean
  - errors[] (blocking)
  - warnings[] (non-blocking)
  - diff_summary (counts + high-risk fields list)
Note: API payload shape is handled in Optimization Config Service ticket; this ticket defines semantics + internal structures.

Implementation plan
- Diff
  - Use JSON pointer-like paths (RFC6901-style) internally; render dotted paths for UI.
  - Normalize objects by sorting keys recursively.
  - For arrays:
    - If array is order-insensitive (explicitly marked in registry), diff as set by stable key (e.g., "regions"), else diff by index.
  - Field registry:
    - Field path -> risk level
    - Field path -> diff mode (set vs list)
    - Field path -> redaction rule (e.g., secrets)
- Semantic validation framework
  - validators as pure functions: (new_config, prev_config, context) -> {errors,warnings,annotations}
  - context includes: deployment_mode, model_id, region, tenant_id, runtime_capabilities snapshot, feature_flags
  - rule IDs for easy on-call search (e.g., VAL-BATCH-001)
- Add unit tests for:
  - diff stability
  - known tricky cases (null vs missing, reordered maps, array order)
  - each validator rule, including "warn" vs "error"

Open questions
- Exact batching bounds: runtime team to confirm final numbers (Noah/Sofia).
- Capability lookup contract: do we query runtime catalog or embed a capability table in control plane? (leans catalog).
- Which fields are UI-redacted vs fully hidden (security review not required for this ticket, but avoid leaking secrets in diffs).

Acceptance criteria
- Diff output is deterministic for equivalent JSON inputs.
- At least 10 semantic rules implemented across batching/cache/quant with unit test coverage.
- /validate (service layer) can surface actionable messages (no generic "invalid config").
- Quant profile change is correctly flagged as high risk and triggers required gate config (error for large scopes; warning for small canary scopes).

References
- PRD: safe apply + rollback requirements (Confluence)
- Design spec: Optimization Config Versioning design (Confluence)
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood/pr-19857-implement-config-diff-validator
- Follow-on: ENG-4824 (canary rollout controller) will consume risk annotations.
comments: 2025-11-13 (Benji Okafor): Drafted validator framework interface + initial diff normalization approach. Planning to use RFC6901 paths internally to avoid ambiguity between dotted keys.

2025-11-14 (Jordan Lee): Please ensure we can classify changes by risk so rollout policy can require canary for “high risk” changes. Quant profile swap should always be high risk by default. Also need consistent rule IDs for policy/audit references.

2025-11-18 (Noah Patel): From runtime perspective: enforce max_batch_tokens upper bound based on hardware class; control plane can implement conservative bounds and runtime can still clamp. Prefer control plane to reject extreme values to avoid worker instability. Also for cache: make sure enabling cache requires cache key includes tokenizer/model hash to avoid poisoning.

2025-11-21 (Arjun Desai): Quant profile validation must check arch + TP degree. If the config points at a profile built for TP=2 but Dedicated cluster is TP=4, that should be a hard error. Also: profiles in “candidate” state should not be customer-visible unless internal flag is on.

2025-12-02 (Benji Okafor): Implemented first pass diff engine + field registry. Added validators: VAL-BATCH-001..004, VAL-CACHE-001..004, VAL-QUANT-001..003. Still need better error copy (include offending path + expected range).

2025-12-05 (Chloe Martin): Console diff view needs a “high risk” banner + list of risky fields. Please include a concise diff_summary (counts + risky paths) so Console doesn’t have to parse full diff to decide UI states.

2025-12-09 (Sean Gallagher): On-call request: warnings/errors must be searchable in logs. Please include rule_id and stable message text (avoid interpolating huge payloads). Also please cap diff value lengths to prevent log blowups.

2025-12-12 (Benji Okafor): Opened PR-19857 with unit tests for stability and validator coverage. Added redaction rule for any field matching /secret|token|key/i in diff output (still shows path + “REDACTED”).

2026-01-07 (Ethan Park): LGTM on approach. Make sure /apply re-validates referenced entities (quant profile, capabilities) to avoid stale validation results. We’ve seen this bite us in other services.

2026-01-10 (Benji Okafor): Merged PR-19857. Follow-up patch added apply-time revalidation hook (service calls validate twice: preflight + pre-commit). Marking ticket done; remaining UX polish is tracked in ENG-4828 (Console diff view).
